scraping.scrape module

scrape.py Scrapes admissions results from GradCafe into a JSON file. Run directly (python scrape.py [options] [output.json]) to scrape; scrape_data and the other functions here can also be imported on their own.

exception scraping.scrape.StopRequested[source]

Bases: BaseException

Raised when a SIGTERM asks a running scrape to stop cleanly. A BaseException rather than an Exception, like KeyboardInterrupt, so it isn’t swallowed by the broad except-Exception retry loops throughout this file.

scraping.scrape.check_robots_allowed(url, user_agent='*')[source]

Check the site’s robots.txt to see if scraping is permitted on the domain. Fetches it with a browser-like User-Agent, since Cloudflare returns a 403 for RobotFileParser’s default “Python-urllib/x.y” UA - which robotparser’s read() treats as “disallow everything” rather than as a fetch failure.

Parameters:

  • url (str) – The URL to check permission for.

  • user_agent (str) – The user agent to check permission for.

Returns:

True if allowed, else False.

Return type:

bool

scraping.scrape.chrome_helper(url, host_port, chrome_bin, profile_dir, retries=5, base_retry_delay=15)[source]

Work around Cloudflare verification at url (GradCafe), using a persistent Chrome profile so a cleared session survives restarts. Retries the initial navigation on transient errors, then only waits for manual completion if a Cloudflare challenge is actually shown. Cleans up its own spawned process if initialization fails partway through.

Parameters:

  • url (str) – The URL to navigate to.

  • host_port (str) – The debugging endpoint’s host:port address.

  • chrome_bin (str or pathlib.Path) – Path to the Chrome binary to launch.

  • profile_dir (str) – Path to the Chrome profile directory to use.

  • retries (int) – How many times to retry the initial navigation.

  • base_retry_delay (int) – Base delay in seconds between retries, doubled on each subsequent attempt.

Returns:

The resulting driver and Chrome process.

Return type:

tuple(selenium.webdriver.Chrome, subprocess.Popen)

scraping.scrape.run_scrape(args)[source]

Scrape GradCafe admissions results into a JSON file.

With –num_results, resumes from saved pagination state and stops at that many total results (or when there are no more pages).

Without –num_results (“pull mode”), always starts at page 1 and ignores saved pagination state, since the goal is to catch newly submitted entries rather than continue an earlier crawl. It stops once –pull_seen_limit consecutive results already exist in the output file (a sign this run has caught up to previously scraped data), when there are no more pages, or when this process receives SIGTERM (as sent by Flask’s Cancel button), whichever comes first. Whatever was already saved before stopping stays saved either way.

Parameters:

args (argparse.Namespace) – Parsed CLI arguments, as returned by parse_args().

Returns:

None.

Return type:

None

scraping.scrape.scrape_data(driver, url=None)[source]

Scrape admissions results from the page at url, or from whatever page is currently loaded if url is None. Clicks “Next” afterward so the following page’s request carries a natural Referer.

Parameters:

  • driver (selenium.webdriver.Chrome) – The active Selenium Chrome driver.

  • url (str or None) – The URL to navigate to, or None to use the current page.

Returns:

A list of Tag objects, each being a row with application details, and the next page’s URL (for resumable state), or None if no next page exists.

Return type:

tuple(list[bs4.Tag], str or None)

scraping.scrape.terminate_process(process, timeout=10)[source]

Terminate the given Chrome process, force-killing it if it doesn’t respond to termination within the timeout. Does not remove the profile directory, since it may be reused across restarts.

Parameters:

  • process (subprocess.Popen) – The Chrome process to terminate.

  • timeout (int) – Seconds to wait for a clean exit before killing it.

Returns:

None.

Return type:

None
